operations.name: Delete background sound
operations.description: Soft-deletes the clip. An agent still naming it in `voice.background_sound.custom_asset_id` falls back to silence for that ambience at its next session rather than failing the call.

operations.name: Delete knowledge folder
operations.description: Delete a folder, empty or not. The knowledge sources inside it are not deleted: they are taken out of the folder (`folder_id` becomes null).

operations.name: Delete knowledge source
operations.description: Delete a knowledge source. Returns 409 while any agent still references it — in its draft or in its currently published version (sessions resolve sources at call time, so deleting a published reference would change a running agent). Check `GET /v1/agent/knowledge-sources/{source_id}/agents`, detach via the agent config, and republish if needed before deleting.

operations.name: Release phone number
operations.description: Release a number back to the provider's inventory and stop its daily billing. This is irreversible: anyone — including other platforms — can buy the number afterwards, so callers who saved it may reach a stranger. The number disappears from this API immediately. 409 while a SIP config update of an imported number is still running, retry shortly.

operations.name: Delete test
operations.description: Delete a test and detach it from every agent. Its past runs stay readable.

operations.name: Delete tool
operations.description: Delete a tool. Returns 409 while any agent's draft configuration still references it — check `GET /v1/agent/tools/{tool_id}/agents` and detach it via the agent config first, so a delete can never silently change agent behavior.

operations.name: Disable tool signing
operations.description: Stop signing this tool's requests and delete its secrets.

operations.name: Revoke previous tool signing secret
operations.description: End a rotation window now. Only the current secret signs from the next session on.

operations.name: Delete (archive) a pronunciation dictionary
operations.description: Soft-archive the dictionary: it disappears from list/get and can no longer be modified, while its versions remain stored. Idempotent.

operations.name: Delete (archive) a version
operations.description: Soft-archive a historical version. The latest version cannot be deleted (409), and deleting an already archived version also returns 409.

operations.name: Rotate tool signing secret
operations.description: Turn on request signing for a webhook tool, or replace its secret. The response returns the new secret once. The replaced secret keeps signing next to the new one for `previous_secret_expires_in_seconds` (default 24 hours), so you can deploy the new secret without dropping a request. Returns 409 while a previous secret is still active: revoke it first. The change reaches every agent using the tool

previous_secret_expires_in_seconds.description: How long the replaced secret keeps signing next to the new one, as a second `v1`. Default 24 hours, at most 7 days. 0 switches at once. Ignored when signing was off.

operations.name: Speech to text
operations.description: Speech to Text

model.description: Specify which speech-to-text model to use.

audio.description: Audio file to be converted to text

language.description: Optional hint. The language is auto-detected regardless; the detected language is returned as `language_code`.

ignore_timestamps.description: Whether to return precise timestamps in the text, this will increase the latency in audio shorter than 30 seconds

operations.name: Audio infill
operations.description: Regenerate part of a recording with drama-3 and get the whole take back. Use it to apply a script change to existing audio without re-recording it: send the take, the full revised `transcript` and the range to replace. drama-3 regenerates that range in the speaker's voice, taken from the audio around it, and returns the take with the new span in place. A request takes one of two shapes. Mixing the

model.description: The model that regenerates the span. Only `drama-3` serves this endpoint.

transcript.description: The full text of the result: the kept audio before the change, the new span and the kept audio after it, with the edit already applied. Sent to the model as written, without text normalization.

audio.description: Edit a take: the whole recording to edit. Requires the start of the span (`prefix_frames` or `prefix_seconds`) and its end (`suffix_frames` or `suffix_seconds`). Do not combine with `prefix_audio` / `suffix_audio`.

prefix_frames.description: Edit a take: the frame where the regenerated span starts. Everything before it is kept. A whole number of frames at 44100 / 2048 (about 21.53) frames per second; 0 keeps nothing before the span. Give this or `prefix_seconds`, not both.

prefix_seconds.description: Edit a take: `prefix_frames` given in seconds from the start of the take, rounded to the nearest frame. Give this or `prefix_frames`, not both.

suffix_frames.description: Edit a take: the frame where the regenerated span ends and the kept audio resumes. Equal to `prefix_frames` inserts new speech at that point; the take's length keeps nothing after the span. Give this or `suffix_seconds`, not both.

suffix_seconds.description: Edit a take: `suffix_frames` given in seconds from the start of the take, rounded to the nearest frame. Give this or `suffix_frames`, not both.

prefix_audio.description: Join two clips: the clip before the generated speech. Alone, the model continues it.

suffix_audio.description: Join two clips: the clip after the generated speech. Requires `prefix_audio`.

sample_rate.description: Audio sample rate in Hz. When null, uses the format's default (44100 Hz for most formats, 48000 Hz for opus).

mp3_bitrate.description: MP3 bitrate in kbps. Only applies when format is mp3.

opus_bitrate.description: Opus bitrate in bps. -1000 for automatic. Only applies when format is opus.

operations.name: Create a pronunciation dictionary
operations.description: Create an empty dictionary for the team the credential belongs to (the API key's team, or the personal team for a session without x-team-id). Publish rules with POST /versions.

name.description: Display name for the dictionary (1-128 characters).

operations.name: Publish a version
operations.description: Publish an immutable snapshot of rules. Send the version you believe is current as `expected_latest_version_id`; a stale value returns 409. Keys are unique within a version (duplicates return 422). Alias rules never shorten billing.

expected_latest_version_id.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard: the latest version ID the caller believes is current, or null for the first publish. A mismatch returns 409.

items.description: Complete ordered rule list for the new version (up to 5000 rules). Keys must be unique within the version; order is the engine's application order.

operations.name: Text to speech
operations.description: Text to Speech

model.description: Specify which TTS model to use. Use `s2.1-pro-free` for the free developer tier. If omitted or set to an unrecognized value, the request falls back to `s2.1-pro`.

temperature.description: Controls expressiveness. Higher is more varied, lower is more consistent.

references.description: Inline voice references for zero-shot cloning. Requires MessagePack (not JSON). For single speaker, provide an array of ReferenceAudio objects. For multiple speakers, provide an array of arrays where each inner array contains references for one speaker. **Multi-speaker is available with the S2 family (`s2-pro`, `s2.1-pro`, `s2.1-pro-free`) and `drama-3`, not `s1`.** The speaker index corresponds t

reference_id.description: Voice model ID(s) from Fish Audio library or your custom models. For single-speaker synthesis, provide a string. For multi-speaker synthesis (dialogue), provide an array of model IDs. **Multi-speaker is available with the S2 family (`s2-pro`, `s2.1-pro`, `s2.1-pro-free`) and `drama-3`, not `s1`.** When using multiple speakers, use speaker tags in your text like `` and `` to indicate speaker change

prosody.description: Speed and volume adjustments for the output.

normalize.description: Rewrites numbers, dates, units and symbols as spoken words before synthesis, improving stability. Uses `language` when it is set and otherwise detects the language of each text chunk.

language.description: BCP-47 language tag of the text, for example `en`, `es-MX` or `zh-CN`. Case-insensitive, and `_` is read as `-`. Used only by text normalization (how numbers, dates, units and symbols are spelled out before synthesis) and by word-timestamp alignment. It is not passed to the speech model and does not change the voice, accent or audio quality; a wrong tag only changes how those tokens are spelled ou

sample_rate.description: Audio sample rate in Hz. When null, uses the format's default (44100 Hz for most formats, 48000 Hz for opus).

mp3_bitrate.description: MP3 bitrate in kbps. Only applies when format is mp3.

opus_bitrate.description: Opus bitrate in bps. -1000 for automatic. Only applies when format is opus.

latency.description: Latency-quality trade-off. normal: best quality, balanced: reduced latency, low: lowest latency.

max_new_tokens.description: Maximum audio tokens to generate per text chunk.

repetition_penalty.description: Penalty for repeating audio patterns. Values above 1.0 reduce repetition.

min_chunk_length.description: Minimum characters before splitting into a new chunk.

condition_on_previous_chunks.description: Use previous audio as context for voice consistency.

early_stop_threshold.description: Early stopping threshold for batch processing.

features.description: Optional request-scoped TTS feature flags forwarded verbatim to the inference backend. Use ["quality-guard"] to enable the quality guard for this synthesis request. Feature availability is determined by the inference backend.

pronunciation_dictionary.description: Optional list of up to 3 pronunciation dictionaries to apply during synthesis. Provide either references to platform-managed dictionaries OR inline literal dictionaries (the two forms are mutually exclusive in a single request). The server resolves and merges the dictionaries, then forwards the full merged dictionary to the inference engine, which performs the substitution. Each entry sets `type`

operations.name: Voice design
operations.description: Voice Design

model.description: Specify which voice-design model to use.

instruction.description: Voice design prompt. Must contain 1 to 2000 characters.

reference_text.description: Optional text used as reference content for the generated voice.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 language hint, such as `en`, `zh`, or `ja`.

n.description: Number of voice candidates to generate.

speed.description: Speaking speed multiplier for candidate generation.

num_step.description: Number of diffusion steps used by the voice-design model.

guidance_scale.description: Classifier-free guidance scale. Higher values follow the prompt more strongly.

instruct_guidance_scale.description: Instruction guidance scale for prompt conditioning.

seed.description: Optional deterministic seed for candidate generation.

operations.name: Attach test
operations.description: Attach a test to an agent so the agent's test runs include it. Attaching an attached test does nothing. The agent and the test must be in the same workspace.

operations.name: Update sip number config
operations.description: Replace the trunk configuration of an imported `sip` number in place: rotate digest credentials, change the allowed source addresses, or add, update and remove the termination host and its custom SIP headers. Send the complete desired configuration; an empty password beside a set username keeps the stored one. Trunk ids are stable across updates, so calls in flight are not affected. 409 for number
